## `clone_github_repository`

*Available in [Python](#clone_github_repository-python)*
=== "Python"
    <h4>Description</h4>
    Clones a GitHub repository via git.
    <h4>Usage</h4>
    ```python
    clone_github_repository(
        repository_url,
        local_path
    )
    ```
    <h4>Arguments</h4>

    - `repository_url` (`str`) - URL of the repository to clone
    - `local_path` (`Path`) - The path where the repository should be cloned.

    <h4>Returns `bool`</h4>

## `create_empty_github_repository`

*Available in [Python](#create_empty_github_repository-python)*
=== "Python"
    <h4>Description</h4>
    Function to create a new empty GitHub repository.
    <h4>Usage</h4>
    ```python
    create_empty_github_repository(
        name,
        description,
        visibility='internal'
    )
    ```
    <h4>Arguments</h4>

    - `name` (`str`) - The name of the repository to create (e.g. https://github.com/CIDA-CSPH/<name>)
    `name` must be a valid URL component (i.e. no spaces, special characters, etc).
    - `description` (`str | None`) - An optional description for the repository. (default: None)
    - `visibility` (`Literal`) - The visibility for the repository (default: 'internal').
    Currently, creating 'public' repositories is not supported to prevent unintentional
    data leakage.

    <h4>Returns `str | None`</h4>

    A URL pointing to the new repository or None

## `create_github_repository`

*Available in [Python](#create_github_repository-python)*
=== "Python"
    <h4>Description</h4>
    Function to create a new GitHub repository.
    This function is intended for interactive use, and is a wrapper around the more specific
    `create_empty_github_repository()` and `create_github_repository_from_template()` functions.

    If you do not need the interactive component (i.e. in a script), call one of those functions instead.
    <h4>Usage</h4>
    ```python
    create_github_repository(
        name,
        description=None,
        visibility='internal',
        template_name=None
    )
    ```
    <h4>Arguments</h4>

    - `name` (`str`) - A name for the repository. (e.g. https://github.com/CIDA-CSPH/<name>)
    - `description` (`str | None`) - An optional description for the repository. (default: None)
    - `visibility` (`Literal`) - The visibility of the new GitHub repo.
    - `template_name` (`str | None`) - The name of the template to use. (default: None)
    If None, will interactively prompt the user to choose a template.
    If 'empty', will create a new empty GitHub repo.
    Otherwise, will attempt to create a GitHub repo with the given template name.

    <h4>Returns `str | None`</h4>

    A string containing the GitHub repository URL, or None if repo creation failed.

## `create_github_repository_from_template`

*Available in [Python](#create_github_repository_from_template-python)*
=== "Python"
    <h4>Description</h4>
    Function to create a new GitHub repository from a template.
    <h4>Usage</h4>
    ```python
    create_github_repository_from_template(
        name,
        template_name,
        description,
        visibility='internal'
    )
    ```
    <h4>Arguments</h4>

    - `name` (`str`) - The name of the repository to create (e.g. https://github.com/CIDA-CSPH/<name>)
    - `template_name` (`str`) - The name of the template repository to use (e.g. CIDA-CSPH/<template_name>)
    - `description` (`str | None`) - An optional description for the repository. (default: None)
    - `visibility` (`Literal`) - The visibility for the repository (default: 'internal')

    <h4>Returns `str | None`</h4>

    A URL pointing to the new repository or None
